clue.text: Lovebirds catching one painful inflammation

indicators.note: the birds hold the next piece inside them, as if catching it

parts.note: read as love (O, the zero score in tennis) plus birds (TITS)
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A pair of lovebirds pick up an infection that turns painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovebirds' must be split into love + birds: O for love, TITS for the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for inflammation of the ear, which is notably painful.

clue.text: Unartistic sound engineering a bloody tragedy!

indicators.note: engineering a sound means working on it and reshaping it, so these letters get rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy sound engineer turns a show into a bloody disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' is literal: Shakespeare's play is famously his goriest tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's early revenge play is notorious for its mutilations and murders, the bloodiest tragedy he wrote.

clue.text: Unevenness in pitch? English right back has second look

indicators.note: sent back, so the two letters for English and right are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mo is a short moment, a second
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: An England right-back takes a second glance at an uneven football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' and 'pitch' suggest football, but 'back' reverses E and RT to TRE, and the pitch is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavering, trembling effect in a note's sound is an unevenness in musical pitch.

clue.text: One's beaten horse, stifling liberal spirit

indicators.note: the horse holds the next letter smothered inside it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A beaten horse suppresses a free spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's beaten' looks like a description of the horse, but it is the definition: a percussion instrument is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean percussion instrument is made from an oil drum and played by being struck with sticks.

clue.text: Lack of talent excluding a privileged group

indicators.note: excluding means one letter is left out of the phrase for lack of talent

parts.note: having no talent is having no ability

explanation.surface: A sneer that an untalented privileged elite keeps others out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats with titles form a privileged class or group in society.

clue.text: Subtle introduction to Nietzsche foxed a dunce

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter
foxed means baffled or confused, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An introductory book on Nietzsche baffles a slow student with its subtlety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with fine shades of meaning is subtle, full of delicate distinctions.

clue.text: President engaged in vacuously boastful clamour

indicators.note: the president's name is engaged, held inside the shell of the next word
a vacuous word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A president caught up in empty, boastful noise.
explanation.definitionFit: After the biblical tower where languages were confused, the word means a confused din or clamour of voices.

clue.text: Chosen to strip off, servicemen stand before the faithful

indicators.note: stripping off the outer layers removes the first and last letters of the synonym for chosen

parts.note: someone chosen by vote is elected
RN is the Royal Navy, servicemen

explanation.surface: Men chosen to serve are told to undress and stand before a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripping takes E and D from the ends of ELECTED, leaving LECTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading desk in a church is a stand placed in front of the congregation of worshippers.

clue.text: In London district, foreign cash goes on drug providing a fix

indicators.note: the cash and drug go in, inside the name of the district

parts.note: Tooting is a district in south London

indicators.note: the cash is followed by the drug, the drug going on after it

parts.note: roubles are Russian currency
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug deal in south London: foreign money changes hands for a fix of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' and 'drug' point to a heroin fix; the fix is solving problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnosing and repairing faults is the business of fixing problems, providing a fix.

clue.text: Swimming seal, then, is somewhere in the Atlantic

indicators.note: the letters swim about, mixing into a new order

explanation.surface: A seal swims out, then finds itself somewhere in the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: This remote island where Napoleon was exiled lies in the South Atlantic Ocean.

clue.text: Stream with no ebbing wave

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a stream

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the word no runs backwards

explanation.surface: A stream whose water never goes out, with no ebb tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like water, but it is the gesture of summoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone with a gesture of the hand is to wave them over.

clue.text: Extremists ejected from industrial action in the capital

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its end letters, which are thrown out

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately slow down

explanation.surface: Militants are thrown out of a workers' protest in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Slimmer's cheese in regional contest

parts.note: low-cal, low in calories, describes a slimmer's food
Derby is an English cheese

explanation.surface: A dieter's cheese entered in a county show competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A match between two neighbouring rival teams from the same area is a regional contest.

clue.text: A French African free from ropes

parts.note: un is French for a
a Moor is a North African

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and an African sailor cast off the ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a boat from the ropes holding it to a mooring is to free it from ropes.

clue.text: Guardian's to hold back, holding back

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to defer is to hold back or postpone
the back of something is its end

explanation.surface: A newspaper is told to hold back while it is holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper; 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: A protector who keeps something safe is a guardian.

clue.text: Lands a few blows in a deceptively promising period

indicators.note: letters that are blown about are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a few punches in a round that only looked promising.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief light before the real sunrise is a deceptively promising moment, an idiom for false hope.

clue.text: What might appeal to cannibal or neoliberal

definitions.meaning: a person cooked in a pan, a meal a man-eater might fancy
Milton, the free-market economist behind monetarism

explanation.surface: A question about what would tempt a man-eater or a free-marketeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a cooked person; as a name it is the Chicago School economist.

clue.text: Insectivore concealed in cane abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and reordered

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: An insect-eating creature hides in the sugar cane in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny Australian anteater feeds on ants and termites, so is an insect-eating animal.

clue.text: Nobody imprisons half a continent in cell

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece locked up inside it

parts.note: none means nobody

indicators.note: half the word for the continent is its first three letters

parts.note: Europe is a continent

explanation.surface: No one locks up half a continent in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' looks like a prison cell, but it is a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell that carries electrical impulses is a type of cell in the body.

clue.text: Shady borders of lime, in which I'm suffering

indicators.note: the edge letters form a container in which the cry is placed
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ouch is a cry meaning I'm in pain

explanation.surface: Sitting in the shade at the edge of a lime tree, I'm in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disreputable or of dubious character is shady.

clue.text: College study, including reading, is a fabulous thing

parts.note: uni is a university or college

indicators.note: the word for study includes the letter for reading inside it

parts.note: to con is to study
R is reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: College study that includes reading is a wonderful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: This one-horned horse is a creature of fable and myth, a fabulous beast.

clue.text: Not charging, in a position like York's welcoming hotel

indicators.note: the phrase welcomes the letter in, holding it within

parts.note: York stands on the River Ouse, so its position is on the Ouse
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A York hotel gives guests a free stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provided free by the establishment, at no charge to the customer, is an idiom for not charging.

clue.text: Beast one very quietly smuggled into house

indicators.note: the pieces are slipped inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A wild animal is sneaked silently into a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a large African beast.

clue.text: On-screen feature suggesting that Apple's ripping you off?

parts.note: Apple names its products with an i prefix, as in iPhone and iPod
a con is a swindle, a rip-off

explanation.surface: A complaint that Apple's on-screen gadgetry is a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an Apple product name, the answer is i + con, a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture on a computer display that you click is an on-screen feature.

clue.text: Frosted desserts, the second sent back

parts.note: an ice is a frozen dessert

indicators.note: sent back means the second dessert is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the second of the desserts is a pud, a pudding

explanation.surface: Iced desserts at a restaurant, with the second one returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desserts' gives two: ICE and PUD; only the second is reversed, to DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a frozen coating, as a windscreen in winter, is frosted.

clue.text: Work accepted by Poirot: a robbery with a twist

indicators.note: a twist turns the letters round so they are read backwards
the letters are taken in by these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Poirot takes on a robbery case with an unexpected twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-scale musical composition for voices and orchestra on a sacred theme is a musical work.

clue.text: Butcher's cut and run, nursing case of lumbago

indicators.note: the first word nurses, holds and cares for, the next piece inside it

parts.note: to cut and run is to flee, to escape

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, first and last letters

explanation.surface: A butcher with back pain cuts and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's cut and run' reads as one action, but the definition is 'Butcher's cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of boneless meat, such as veal, is a cut that a butcher prepares.

clue.text: Silver service's passed round for youth

indicators.note: the service is passed round the metal, enclosing it

parts.note: none, or nones, is the church service at the ninth hour
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver tableware handed round at a dinner, for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: None is the monastic office said at the ninth hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal minority, the time of being under age, is a period of youth.
